rows.subtopic: Deciding whether to quit or persist
rows.subtype: Approach: decide to stay with a set review and adjust [Revision]
rows.description: After the trial, the person chooses to stay for six more months with a written goal for skills and pay, and a scheduled review. If the goal is missed, the exit plan is ready.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, contingency planning, cutting losses, experiment and measure, pros and cons, rigid persistence

rows.subtopic: Deciding whether to quit or persist
rows.subtype: Approach: ask what would change the decision [Thinking]
rows.description: The person writes three conditions under which staying makes sense, such as a promotion path or a team change, and checks whether they can happen. Clear criteria make the choice less emotional.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, contingency planning, cutting losses, experiment and measure, pros and cons, rigid persistence

rows.subtopic: Deciding whether to quit or persist
rows.subtype: Approach: switch to a lighter plan when burned out [Revision]
rows.description: Facing burnout, the person takes planned leave, drops a side project and revisits the decision after rest. Recovering first improves the quality of a later choice.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, cutting losses, experiment and measure, pros and cons, rigid persistence, root cause analysis

rows.subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
rows.subtype: Approach: list all demands and rank them by urgency and importance [Thinking]
rows.description: A final-year student lists hospital visits, exams, assignments and household tasks, and decides that treatment appointments and the coming exam are the top priorities. Ranking gives a way to say no to the rest.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, commitment device, contingency planning, time-boxing

rows.subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
rows.subtype: Approach: share the care schedule with siblings and relatives [Action]
rows.description: The student writes a weekly rota for hospital stays, medicine pickup and cooking and asks a sibling, an aunt and a neighbour to take fixed slots. Sharing the care prevents burnout of one person.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, commitment device, contingency planning, prioritising

rows.subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
rows.subtype: Approach: take on everything alone to prove devotion [Pitfall]
rows.description: Feeling that asking for help is disloyal, the student does every task and sleeps four hours. Exhaustion leads to a failed test and short temper, which makes the care worse.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, commitment device, contingency planning, prioritising, time-boxing

rows.subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
rows.subtype: Approach: talk to teachers about accommodations [Action]
rows.description: The student explains the situation to the department head and asks for deadline flexibility and a chance to attend class notes online. Most institutions have some provision if asked early.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, contingency planning, prioritising, time-boxing

rows.subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
rows.subtype: Approach: contingency plan for a hospital emergency [Thinking]
rows.description: The student prepares a folder with prescriptions, reports and insurance papers, saves the doctor's number, and agrees with relatives on who travels if the condition worsens. Preparing removes scramble in a crisis.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, commitment device, prioritising, time-boxing

rows.subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
rows.subtype: Approach: study in small blocks around the caregiving day [Action]
rows.description: The student uses waiting-room hours and bus rides for revision using short notes, and keeps one fixed hour at night for hard topics. Time-boxing turns broken time into usable study.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, commitment device, contingency planning, prioritising

rows.subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
rows.subtype: Approach: notice signs of caregiver fatigue and step back [Revision]
rows.description: Realising that irritation and poor sleep are constant, the student asks an aunt to take two nights and books a counselling session. Recognising limits keeps the care sustainable.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, commitment device, contingency planning, prioritising, time-boxing
